title: Pasting two forward left-coefficient tensor actions
statement:
Use monoidal categories [def-sfb-monoidal-category] with associator $\alpha:(U\otimes V)\otimes W\to U\otimes(V\otimes W)$ and left unitor $\lambda$. A strong monoidal functor has the structure of [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]; write $\delta^H_{U,V}:H(U\otimes V)\xrightarrow{\sim}HU\otimes HV$ and $e_H:H\mathbf1\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1$ for its inverse structure maps. Set $h^H_N=\lambda_N\circ(e_H\otimes1_N)$ and $a^H_{B,B',N}=\alpha_{HB,HB',N}\circ(\delta^H_{B,B'}\otimes1_N)$. Composition is right to left.
Let $\mathcal C_0,\mathcal C_1,\mathcal C_2$ be monoidal categories. Let $F:\mathcal C_0\to\mathcal C_1$ and $Q:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_2$ be strong monoidal, and let $R:\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_0$, $J:\mathcal C_2\to\mathcal C_1$ be arbitrary functors. Set $S=QF$, $P=RJ$, with the composite inverse comparisons
$$\delta^S_{B,B'}=\delta^Q_{FB,FB'}\circ Q(\delta^F_{B,B'}),\qquad e_S=e_Q\circ Q(e_F).$$
Suppose given natural transformations
$$t_{B,N}:B\otimes RN\to R(FB\otimes N),\qquad v_{C,M}:C\otimes JM\to J(QC\otimes M)$$
for $B\in\mathcal C_0$, $N,C\in\mathcal C_1$, $M\in\mathcal C_2$. Require that for each pair $(H,K,w)=(F,R,t)$ and $(Q,J,v)$, and all appropriately typed $D,D',L$, the following two equations hold:
$$K(h^H_L)\circ w_{\mathbf1,L}=\lambda_{KL},$$
$$K(a^H_{D,D',L})\circ w_{D\otimes D',L}=w_{D,HD'\otimes L}\circ(1_D\otimes w_{D',L})\circ\alpha_{D,D',KL}.$$
Define the specified composite
$$T_{B,M}=R(v_{FB,M})\circ t_{B,JM}:B\otimes PM\longrightarrow P(SB\otimes M).$$
Then $T$ is natural in both variables and satisfies
$$P(h^S_M)\circ T_{\mathbf1,M}=\lambda_{PM},$$
$$P(a^S_{B,B',M})\circ T_{B\otimes B',M}=T_{B,SB'\otimes M}\circ(1_B\otimes T_{B',M})\circ\alpha_{B,B',PM}.$$
No adjunction, symmetry, invertibility of $t,v,T$, or geometric composition law is assumed.

proof.text:
Unpack the specified composite comparisons, using tensor bifunctoriality [def-sfb-monoidal-category] and the functor and inverse-structure-map conventions [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Direct substitution gives
$$h^S_M=h^Q_M\circ(Q(e_F)\otimes1_M),\qquad a^S_{B,B',M}=a^Q_{FB,FB',M}\circ(Q(\delta^F_{B,B'})\otimes1_M).$$
Indeed the first is $\lambda_M(e_Q\otimes1)(Q(e_F)\otimes1)=\lambda_M((e_Q Q(e_F))\otimes1)$; the second is $\alpha_{QFB,QFB',M}(\delta^Q_{FB,FB'}\otimes1)(Q(\delta^F_{B,B'})\otimes1)$. These use only the two comparison formulas in the hypotheses; no coherence theorem for composing monoidal functors is invoked.

proof.text:
For morphisms $b:B\to\widetilde B$ in $\mathcal C_0$ and $m:M\to\widetilde M$ in $\mathcal C_2$, naturality of the assumed $v$ and then of the assumed $t$ gives
$$\begin{aligned}
P(Sb\otimes m)\circ T_{B,M}
&=R\bigl(J(QF b\otimes m)\circ v_{FB,M}\bigr)\circ t_{B,JM}\\
&=R(v_{F\widetilde B,\widetilde M})\circ R(Fb\otimes Jm)\circ t_{B,JM}\\
&=R(v_{F\widetilde B,\widetilde M})\circ t_{\widetilde B,J\widetilde M}\circ(b\otimes RJm)
=T_{\widetilde B,\widetilde M}\circ(b\otimes Pm).
\end{aligned}$$
Functoriality and the tensor bifunctor laws justify combining the two variables [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor, def-sfb-monoidal-category]. This proves naturality in both variables.

proof.text:
Naturality of $v$ in its coefficient at $e_F:F\mathbf1\to\mathbf1$ says
$$J(Q(e_F)\otimes1_M)\circ v_{F\mathbf1,M}=v_{\mathbf1,M}\circ(e_F\otimes1_{JM}).$$
Using Step 1 and the assumed unit equations, first for $v$ and then for $t$, gives
$$\begin{aligned}
P(h^S_M)\circ T_{\mathbf1,M}
&=R\bigl(J(h^Q_M)\circ v_{\mathbf1,M}\circ(e_F\otimes1_{JM})\bigr)\circ t_{\mathbf1,JM}\\
&=R\bigl(\lambda_{JM}\circ(e_F\otimes1_{JM})\bigr)\circ t_{\mathbf1,JM}\\
&=R(h^F_{JM})\circ t_{\mathbf1,JM}=\lambda_{RJM}.
\end{aligned}$$
The regrouping is just preservation of composition by $R,J$ and tensor bifunctoriality [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor, def-sfb-monoidal-category]. In particular $F\mathbf1$ is not identified definitionally with $\mathbf1$.

proof.text:
Fix $B,B',M$, put $A=FB$, $D=FB'$, $d=\delta^F_{B,B'}:F(B\otimes B')\to A\otimes D$, and denote the left side of the required associativity equality by $E=P(a^S_{B,B',M})\circ T_{B\otimes B',M}$. Naturality of the assumed $v$ at the coefficient morphism $d$ is
$$J(Qd\otimes1_M)\circ v_{F(B\otimes B'),M}=v_{A\otimes D,M}\circ(d\otimes1_{JM}).$$
Substitute this and Step 1 into $E$ to obtain
$$E=R\bigl(J(a^Q_{A,D,M})\circ v_{A\otimes D,M}\bigr)\circ R(d\otimes1_{JM})\circ t_{B\otimes B',JM}.$$
This is one naturality square, followed by functorial reassociation [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor, def-sfb-monoidal-category].

proof.text:
Apply the assumed associativity equation for $v$ at $(A,D,M)$ in the expression of Step 4:
$$J(a^Q_{A,D,M})\circ v_{A\otimes D,M}=v_{A,QD\otimes M}\circ(1_A\otimes v_{D,M})\circ\alpha_{A,D,JM}.$$
By the definition in the item, $\alpha_{A,D,JM}\circ(d\otimes1_{JM})=a^F_{B,B',JM}$. Combining these adjacent factors inside $R$ gives
$$E=R(v_{A,QD\otimes M})\circ R(1_A\otimes v_{D,M})\circ R(a^F_{B,B',JM})\circ t_{B\otimes B',JM}.$$
Only functoriality and the displayed associator convention are used [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor, def-sfb-monoidal-category].

proof.text:
Use the assumed associativity equation for $t$ at $(B,B',JM)$:
$$R(a^F_{B,B',JM})\circ t_{B\otimes B',JM}=t_{B,D\otimes JM}\circ(1_B\otimes t_{B',JM})\circ\alpha_{B,B',RJM}.$$
Its substitution into Step 5 yields
$$E=R(v_{A,QD\otimes M})\circ R(1_A\otimes v_{D,M})\circ t_{B,D\otimes JM}\circ(1_B\otimes t_{B',JM})\circ\alpha_{B,B',RJM}.$$
Every object is in $\mathcal C_0$ after applying $R$ where indicated; this is substitution into a composite, with tensor and functor conventions from [def-sfb-monoidal-category, def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor].

proof.text:
Naturality of $t$ in its second variable at the $\mathcal C_1$-morphism $v_{D,M}:D\otimes JM\to J(QD\otimes M)$ says
$$R(1_A\otimes v_{D,M})\circ t_{B,D\otimes JM}=t_{B,J(QD\otimes M)}\circ(1_B\otimes R(v_{D,M})).$$
Insert it into Step 6. The first two factors are now $R(v_{A,QD\otimes M})\circ t_{B,J(QD\otimes M)}=T_{B,QD\otimes M}$, and tensor bifunctoriality combines the next two factors into $1_B\otimes(R(v_{D,M})\circ t_{B',JM})=1_B\otimes T_{B',M}$. Thus
$$E=T_{B,SB'\otimes M}\circ(1_B\otimes T_{B',M})\circ\alpha_{B,B',PM},$$
since $QD=SB'$ and $RJ=P$. This proves the asserted associativity by the given naturality square, preservation of composition, and tensor bifunctoriality [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor, def-sfb-monoidal-category].
